The test is short and self-contained (<10 lines) and does not duplicate setup across multiple methods. No helper methods are necessary for this single test and there is no repeated code.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: Method is small (<20 lines) with linear flow, no loops or complex conditionals; cyclomatic complexity is low and it follows a simple Arrange-Act-Assert pattern.
The test makes two concrete assertions verifying multiple properties (edge existence and vertex count), which increases fault-detection capability compared to a single superficial assertion.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations and no commented-out test methods; the test is active and runnable.

No annotations or Javadoc link the test or method to a requirement/ticket ID; the class-level comment mentions traceability but there are no explicit REQ-/JIRA-/US- identifiers or @Story/@Issue annotations tied to this method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes a @Test(timeout = 4000) annotation, which is an explicit performance-related constraint; therefore the class contains an explicit timing-based test.
The method name is generic ('test7') and does not describe the scenario or expected result; it does not follow descriptive naming conventions like method_condition_expectedResult.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: Signs of generated test artifacts are present: the test name 'test7', use of EvoSuite runner and scaffolding class indicate auto-generated patterns rather than minimal, intention-revealing code.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test appears to be a single basic scenario with no Given-When-Then structure in the method and no evidence of broader scenario prioritization or BDD-style design; test design appears minimal and after-the-fact.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises only public APIs (constructor and public methods) and does not use reflection or access private fields, avoiding tight coupling to implementation details.

Assertions do not include descriptive failure messages and there are only two assertions but neither includes messages; rule prefers descriptive messages and specific assertions with messages for easier diagnosis.
The file contains concise class-level comments that explain intent and no excessive inline comments or commented-out code; there is no commented-out test code visible in the method.
The test does not use Random, current time, sleeps, or external dependencies; it performs deterministic operations on an in-memory Grafo instance, so results should be deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses only local in-memory objects and does not persist files, modify static globals, or rely on external resources; no cleanup is required.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing a label that enables selecting this test class as a unit test category.
